all_solved_problems.title: Sort Colors
all_solved_problems.notes: Interview Mode, Phase 1 (new technique, no timer). 3-gate failed (couldn't justify two-pointer) → First Principles path. Solved BOTH approaches. APPROACH 1 — counting sort (his brute force, reached via lifelines): Counter(nums) one pass to count 0s/1s/2s, then a SEPARATE write-index marches left→right painting 0s, then 1s, then 2s in place. Self-reached realizations: (a) values are ONLY {0,1,2} = the unlock; (b) ascending order is forced by CHOOSING to write 0 first, NOT by hashmap iteration (caught his own bug: Counter encounter-order ≠ ascending); (c) count and write are TWO separate passes, not simultaneous — after counting, original array is dead; (d) one shared write-index advances per placement (caught the bug where a per-loop counter restarts at 0 → would overwrite earlier values); (e) do NOT clear()/reset — nums[i]= on an empty list is IndexError; existing slots ARE the canvas; (f) return NOTHING, mutate in place; (g) Counter returns 0 for missing key (no KeyError, unlike plain dict; defaultdict(int) also returns 0 but inserts the key; cleanest = fixed list [0,0,0] indexed by value). Time O(n), space O(1). APPROACH 2 — Dutch National Flag one-pass follow-up, DERIVED FROM SCRATCH via lifelines (Wiganz chose 'grind it' over being shown). three pointers left/mid/right; mid scans; nums[mid]==0 → swap with left, left++ mid++; ==1 → mid++; ==2 → swap with right, right-- and MID STAYS. THE subtlety he discovered himself: 2-swap brings a value from the UNEXPLORED right zone = unchecked → mid stays to examine it; 0-swap brings a value from BEHIND mid (already-scanned, all 1s) = already checked → mid advances. Loop `while mid <= right` — he first guessed `<`, then TESTED [1,0] and saw index-1's 0 never processes → fixed to `<=`. THIS IS HIS DOCUMENTED BINARY-SEARCH BOUNDARY WEAKNESS, self-corrected by tracing the edge case = real healing. Code self-scan bugs caught: len(n)→len(nums); `if mid==2`→`elif nums[mid]==2` (index vs VALUE); three separate ifs→if/elif/else chain (the 1-case was falling through into the else swap); missing colon on else. Pedagogy note: hit a hard 'don't understand a single thing' wall on the mid-stays subtlety → recovered fully via dead-simple two-box [2,1] reframe, then derived the rest himself. Archive + HTML + Patterns entry generated by leetcode-archivist.

finding left/right boundary (CRITICAL — see Time-Based KV #981)

floor vs ceil mid choice — caused infinite loop in Time-Based KV. RULE: the pointer that assigns `= mid` (no ±1) is the only one that can freeze. `left = mid` + floor mid stalls → use CEIL mid (l+r+1)//2. `right = mid` + floor mid is safe (First Bad/Find Peak).
right = len vs len-1 in bisect template (boundaries-between-elements vs index)
aha_moments: ROTATED ARRAY INVARIANT (#33): an invariant = a promise always true no matter what. Normal sorted array's promise = 'the whole thing is sorted' → that's what makes throwing away half SAFE. Rotation BREAKS that promise (7→0 cliff). The surviving promise: 'when you split at mid, AT LEAST ONE of the two halves is always fully sorted' (counter-test [5,6,7,0,1,2,4] split at idx3 → left [5,6,7,0] NOT sorted, right [1,2,4] sorted → proves 'at least one', not 'both'). So the algorithm MUST first detect WHICH half is sorted (nums[left]<=nums[mid] → left sorted), because only the sorted half restores the trustworthy range check. Then: target in sorted-half range → hunt there; else throw that half away.

PROCESS LESSON (#33 audit): a CORRECT answer can still hide a broken process. Discovery work (algorithm/rules/invariant) belongs in 4P Reason — NOT Step 1 (which only confirms WHAT is asked). Doing discovery in Step 1 means the invariant never gets delivered to 4P-C where it's needed (he wrote 'I DON'T KNOW' there despite having already found it).
floor mid (l+r)//2 always rounds DOWN toward left → mid lives on left's side. With `left = mid` and adjacent pointers, left = mid = left → no movement → INFINITE LOOP.
Fix 1: CEIL mid (l+r+1)//2 pushes mid toward right so `left = mid` advances. Fix 2 (preferred): use bisect template left=mid+1 / right=mid with floor mid — both branches always shrink, never loops.
Two mirror templates: `left=mid` (ceil, answer at values[left]) vs `left=mid+1` (floor, answer at values[left-1]).

Bisect template: left ends = COUNT of elements <= t = first index where ts > t. left==0 → none valid → ''. right=len (not len-1) because left/right are boundaries between elements (0..len); only values[mid] is ever read and mid < right ≤ len so always in-bounds.
left==0 guard also blocks Python values[-1] silent wrap-around.
Why First Bad/Find Peak never worry about infinite loop: they use `right = mid` (safe with floor), not `left = mid`.

knapsack.notes: Linear DP understood. Coin Change extends to Unbounded Knapsack — coin reusable, iterate amount outer + coins inner (NOT reverse). dp[0]=0, rest=inf.
aha_moments: Unbounded Knapsack: same item reusable → iterate amount outer, coins inner. 0/1 Knapsack: iterate amount in REVERSE to prevent reuse.
dp[i] = min(dp[i], dp[i-coin]+1) — only update if coin <= amount AND dp[i-coin] != inf

problems: Search In Rotated Array (#33) — REDO / process audit
recent_sessions.aha_moment: THE INVARIANT, rebuilt from scratch: normal sorted array's promise = 'whole thing is sorted' (what makes throwing half away safe). Rotation breaks it (7→0 cliff). Surviving promise = 'when split at mid, AT LEAST ONE half is always fully sorted' (counter-tested [5,6,7,0,1,2,4] → only right half sorted). So detect WHICH half is sorted FIRST (nums[left]<=nums[mid]) — 'only the sorted half can I trust the range check on.'
recent_sessions.process_findings: Solo code 100% CORRECT, 0 bugs — but 3 PROCESS findings: (T1) Step1 'Trace' derived the whole algorithm = boundary violation, belongs in 4P Reason; (T2) 4P-C invariant 'I DON'T KNOW' = same wound as T1 (found it in wrong room, never delivered); (T3) Verify = one happy path, no edge cases. Meta-lesson: a correct answer can still hide a broken process.

Naive parent-only BST check fails ancestor violations. Pass (min_val, max_val) bounds down every recursive call — bounds tighten at each step (left: max=parent.val, right: min=parent.val). Space O(h) not O(n): call stack depth = path length = tree height.
Topological Sort via Kahn's BFS. in-degree map + adjacency list. Queue starts with 0-in-degree nodes. Cycle = processed count < numCourses.
